subjects.description: small green rectangular block attached to bottom of vertical spring

observation.what_happens: A small green block hung from a vertical spring oscillates up and down in the center of the frame. The motion starts with the block low near the striped bar, rises and then continues oscillating vertically through the end of the clip.

calibration.note: no scale: lengths are in pixels

reasoning: The s channel shows ~0.7 s period vertical oscillation about ~95 pix with amplitude decaying from ~80 to ~30 pix, classic damped spring-mass. x stays near zero so motion is 1D along s. Candidates go from ideal to viscous damping to quadratic air drag and cubic stiffness to test decay shape and linearity on unseen data.

critique.finding: The block rides a spring that stiffens as it stretches, centered near {s_eq} with hum {omega}, friction {gamma} and extra stiffening {alpha}.
critique.headline: Spring block bounces with stiffening pull and soft damping
critique.why_it_won: The cubic stiffening lets it stay in step on big and small swings while plain linear springs drift out of step and miss by far.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, its round named before it existed: a hardening spring with viscous damping. Found by Muse Spark's own law, every constant within 0.5σ.
finding: A damped spring that gets a little stiffer or softer on big stretches. Measured: linear natural angular frequency 7.8587 ± 0.0022 1/s; equilibrium position along track 97.68 ± 0.11 pix; linear viscous damping rate 0.57140 ± 0.00080 1/s.

eyeball.law_in_words: vertical block position x obeys damped oscillator about equilibrium s_eq: x'' = -omega0^2*(x-s_eq) - gamma*x' - alpha*(x-s_eq)^3, filmed from side, 42.9 fps for 300 frames

clockCheck.why: Clock not checked: with no ruler in view and no length stated, gravity can’t be measured in metres. A slowed clip would look the same.

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6606499). The round was named in 078bdc5 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in 3d5237d before the clip was rendered; the run used commit 6514586 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in cd70ce2. Found. The drawn law was a cubic hardening spring with viscous damping and no drive. Muse Spark's own Duffing law with viscous damping won: natural frequency 7.8587 ± 0.0022 rad/s against 7.8581 (0.3σ), damping 0.5714 ± 0.0008 against 0.571 (0.5σ), cubic 2995 ± 7 against 2991.5 per m² s² (0.5σ). The referee accepted it, so Muse Wonder was not called. The residual spectrum of the best law without a drive had no peak above the noise, so no drive was offered and none was written: no false drive. Code's dry-friction variant of the winner ranked second, far behind. It predicts the unseen frames to 1.2 times the noise. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner (Muse Spark): linear (ω₀), viscous γ = 0.57140 ± 0.00080 (713σ, present), cubic α = 0.0052184 ± 0.000012 (423σ, present); drawn: linear, cubic, viscous. Term sets equal.
